name: Release a claimed match
description: NOT A FAULT AND NOT A LAPSE. A runner calls this when it cannot play a row -- the usual cause is a model its own roster clock has not registered yet -- and the row goes back to the queue with a refusal spent rather than a strike. The ceiling is what stops a runner that is permanently behind passing one row round the fleet for ever: at the third refusal the row fails as MODEL_UNAVAILABLE and says so, which is a diagnosable end. refusals and lapses are counted apart because they mean different things about the fleet.

input.query: UPDATE matches SET status = CASE WHEN refusals + 1 >= ($3)::int THEN 'failed' ELSE 'pending' END::match_status, refusals = refusals + 1, claim_token = NULL, lease_expires_at = NULL, fault_reason = CASE WHEN refusals + 1 >= ($3)::int THEN 'MODEL_UNAVAILABLE' END, closed_at = CASE WHEN refusals + 1 >= ($3)::int THEN now() END WHERE id = ($5)::uuid AND claim_token = ($1)::uuid AND status = 'claimed' AND ($2)::boolean AND played_by = ($4)::uuid AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM live_runners lr WHERE lr.id = ($4)::uuid)

with.name: The claim is gone
with.description: Nothing to release means the row was already taken back -- by the reap, or by another attempt. The runner's answer is the same either way: claim again.

tasks.name: Read what became of the row
tasks.description: The runner is told whether its refusal was the one that failed the row, because a refusal that ends a match is worth logging loudly at the edge and an ordinary one is not.

input.query: SELECT json_build_object('released', true, 'refusals', m.refusals, 'failed', m.status = 'failed', 'fault_reason', m.fault_reason) AS body FROM matches m WHERE m.id = ($1)::uuid
